verdict.rationale: Framer documents its own first-party 'External Agent' connection that gives Claude Code, Cursor and Codex direct access to the canvas, components, CMS and project context. Agent changes land on a reviewable branch. Framer presents this as its answer to a 'Framer MCP' but states it 'doesn't require a separate MCP server', so the evidence never confirms it is a standard MCP server endpoint. missing for 10: explicit confirmation of an official MCP server/endpoint, documented setup/protocol details and tool list, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: If you’re searching for a Framer MCP, the native Framer External Agent connection gives Claude Code, Cursor, Codex... direct access to your canvas, components, CMS, and project context, without manual MCP setup.
Framer works directly with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other AI tools. Native access to Framer with your own AI agents
Once connected, the agent can read and write CMS collections, including creating, updating, and deleting items.
every change made by an external agent automatically happens on a branch
